chapter_name: Planning and Sustainable Development in Indian Context
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how the government plans for equitable growth across regions and how we can develop without destroying the environment!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The process of thinking, formulating schemes, and implementing them to achieve economic and social goals. In India, it is done through Sectoral planning (agriculture, industry) and Regional planning (focusing on backward areas).
Because development is uneven, special programs target specific areas (like Hill Area Development, Drought Prone Area Program) or specific groups (Small Farmers Development Agency).
A tribal area in Himachal Pradesh (Gaddi tribe). Planning here focused on building schools, healthcare, and roads, vastly improving literacy and reducing gender inequality.
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It balances economic, social, and ecological goals.
A massive canal bringing water to the dry Thar Desert in Rajasthan. While it boosted agriculture and greenery, over-irrigation is causing waterlogging and soil salinity (ecological problems).

fun_activity.title: Mayor for a Day
fun_activity.instructions: If you were given 1 crore rupees to 'plan' the development of your neighborhood, how much would you allocate to roads, parks, schools, and water supply? Make a sustainable budget!

exam_tips: 📌 The concept of 'Sustainable Development' gained momentum after the Brundtland Commission Report (Our Common Future) in 1987.
📌 Be ready to analyze the positive and negative impacts of the Indira Gandhi Canal command area.
📌 Understand why Hill Area and Drought Prone area programs were initiated (to remove regional imbalances).
quick_recap: ⭐ Regional planning aims to reduce economic disparities between different states and districts.
⭐ The ITDP (Integrated Tribal Development Project) in Bharmaur drastically improved the quality of life for the Gaddi tribe.
⭐ Sustainable development requires a strict balance between economic growth and environmental conservation.
